title: Master of Criminal Law (I) (Col to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC
raw_text:
7.     MOS 4409, Master of Criminal Law (I) (Col to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. A Master of Criminal Law has specialized education or
skills in criminal law or military justice.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Must be a field grade officer. Judge Advocates who obtain the
necessary LL.M. or equivalent educational experience as a captain will not
receive the additional MOS until promoted to the rank of major. In addition,
must either:

            (a) Hold a Master of Laws degree (LL.M.) in criminal law from an
American Bar Association accredited program at a civilian institution
approved by Judge Advocate Division.

            (b) Successfully complete a specialty program in criminal law
from the Graduate Course at The Judge Advocate General’s Legal Center and
School, U.S. Army, including completion of all degree requirements for an
LL.M.

            (c) Successfully complete a CCLEB, CPIB, or TLS selected
fellowship related to criminal law or military justice established with a
civilian department or agency through coordination between Judge Advocate
Division, MMOA, and the external department or agency.

        (2) Must be a field grade officer. Judge advocates who meet the
other prerequisite as a captain will not receive the additional MOS until
promoted to the rank of major.

    c. Requirements. Judge Advocate Division, in conjunction with DC, M&RA
(MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS.

       d.   Duties

            (1) May serve in any other MOS 4402 billet.

        (2) Serve in billets requiring an expertise in military and criminal
law issues. This includes litigation positions, as well as policy and
counsel assistance positions at Judge Advocate Division or the Office of the
Judge Advocate General of the Navy.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Lawyers 23-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
